title: Venture Lapland takes majority control of the luxury travel group Arctra
seoTitle: Arctra: Venture Lapland buys into Rovaniemi luxury
description: The investment company Venture Lapland has bought a majority holding in the Rovaniemi luxury travel group Arctra and plans to build more capacity near the city.
dek: The plan is to multiply the group's revenue roughly tenfold, add luxury accommodation floor space near Rovaniemi and grow services from lodging to transport, security and concierge.
heroAlt: A pale blue winter panorama of frozen lakes, snow-covered spruce forest and distant fells in Finnish Lapland.
heroCaption: Winter in Finnish Lapland, seen from Riisitunturi in Posio; Rukatunturi in the distance. The picture is scenery of the region, not of any property named in this story.

body.text: Venture Lapland, an investment company that backs northern growth firms, has acquired a majority holding in Arctra, a luxury travel group based in Rovaniemi, and says it intends to multiply the group's revenue roughly tenfold. The two companies announced the deal on 16.9.2026. Arctra continues under its own name.

Arctra is not a LaplandVibes partner. We are paid nothing for this story and earn nothing from the company. It is here because it changes what can be booked in the Rovaniemi area in the coming seasons.

Arctra is built from four units. Arctra DMC is the travel agency: it brings international customers to Lapland and runs the service production, from cooks to guides. Otava Lodge is the group's own luxury accommodation. Divánta is the concierge house, handling privacy and close protection, and LuxCar is the luxury car rental with its own vehicles and drivers. According to the release the group employs just over 40 people during the winter season.
“Arctra's four business areas are the first in Finland to offer a complete range of services for luxury travel,” says Elias Joentakanen, chairman of the board of Venture Lapland.

The release gives the group's revenue for its latest financial year as a pro forma figure, and sets out the target once a multi-year investment programme is finished. The difference between the two is where the word tenfold comes from.

body.title: Revenue now, and the target after the investment programme
body.text: Both figures are the company's own, from the release of 16 September. The target is an estimate, not a result.

The growth is to come from new accommodation capacity and a wider range of services. The release says the added floor space will be built near Rovaniemi, and names lodging, transport, security and concierge work as the services being expanded.

“The investment programme brings 6,000 square metres of new luxury-level accommodation capacity to the Rovaniemi area, and after that our goal is to employ around 200 luxury travel professionals,” says Petri Juotasniemi, technical director.
What this means for the coming seasons

For the 2026–2027 season the group says its sales are clearly ahead of the same point last year. It also points to the expanded Rovaniemi airport, which it says serves customers arriving by private aircraft.
“Christmas is already almost sold out. Many of our customers book their next trip while the current one is still running,” Joentakanen says.
Every villa and lodge we list in Lapland, with the season each one is open, is in our collection.
body.label: The villa collection

body.text: The release does not say when the new capacity opens, where exactly it will stand beyond “near Rovaniemi”, or what any of it will cost. Until those are published, nothing new from this programme can be booked.
